title: Before He Was A Pirate, Johnny Depp Was Basically A Rock Star Who Kept Accidentally Becoming A Movie Star
dek: Forget the eyeliner and the compass — this is the version of Johnny Depp who quit school to play guitar, hated his own teen-idol TV show, and turned down blockbuster after blockbuster just to work with the weirdest directors he could find.

items.heading: He Dropped Out Of High School To Chase A Record Deal, Not A Movie Career
items.text: Depp left school at 16 to become a rock musician, playing guitar in a Florida band called The Kids before the group relocated to Los Angeles hoping to land a record contract. Acting wasn't even on the radar yet — music was the whole plan, and it stayed his other career for the next four decades.

images.caption: Long before Pirates, Depp was a teenage guitarist chasing a record deal.

items.heading: He Basically Fell Into Acting By Accident, Thanks To Nicolas Cage
items.text: With the band going nowhere, Depp's then-wife introduced him to her friend Nicolas Cage, who suggested he try acting and got him in front of an agent. That connection led straight to his film debut as a teenager killed in his own bed in Wes Craven's A Nightmare on Elm Street.

images.caption: Cage nudged a broke musician named Johnny Depp toward acting.

items.heading: He Didn't Even Want The Role That Made Him Famous
items.text: When 21 Jump Street came calling in 1987, Depp had just wrapped Platoon and had zero interest in signing on to serialized TV. He took the part anyway, became an overnight teen idol, and by his own admission grew increasingly miserable playing undercover cop Tom Hanson for four seasons.

images.caption: The reluctant teen idol of 21 Jump Street.
He'd just wrapped this when Jump Street came knocking.

items.heading: Edward Scissorhands Was The Moment He Stopped Being A Teen Idol And Started Being An Actor
items.text: Determined to shed his heartthrob image, Depp turned to eccentric directors instead of mainstream fame, and his performance as Tim Burton's gentle, blade-fingered outsider became the film that established him as one of Hollywood's most sought-after talents. It also kicked off a director-actor partnership that would eventually span eight movies together.

images.caption: The film that rebranded him from teen idol to serious actor.
The start of a legendary creative partnership.

items.heading: He Turned Down A Movie That Made Someone Else A '90s Action Icon
items.text: While plenty of actors would've jumped at guaranteed box office gold, Depp passed on the lead in Point Break, and the role went to Patrick Swayze instead. He was famously unbothered chasing blockbuster money, once flatly declaring, "I'm not blockbuster boy... I never wanted to be."

images.caption: The role Depp passed on — Swayze took it and never looked back.
He got the part Depp turned down.

items.heading: He Skipped A Guaranteed Blockbuster To Make A Movie That Bombed — On Purpose
items.text: In 1994, Depp chose to shoot Tim Burton's black-and-white passion project Ed Wood instead of cashing in elsewhere, and the film flopped hard, pulling in under $6 million against an $18 million budget. It didn't matter — Ed Wood went on to earn Martin Landau a Best Supporting Actor Oscar and is now considered one of Burton's most acclaimed films, proof Depp's gamble on weird over safe kept paying off critically even when it didn't pay off financially.

images.caption: A box-office bomb that became a cult classic.
Won an Oscar for the film Depp chose over a paycheck.

items.heading: Three Oscar Nominations, Zero Wins — And He Says He's Totally Fine With That
items.text: Depp has been nominated for Best Actor three times: for playing Captain Jack Sparrow in Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl, real-life author J.M. Barrie in Finding Neverland, and the title role in Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street. He's lost all three, but has said he never actually wanted to win: "A nomination is plenty."

items.heading: The Music Career Never Actually Stopped — It Just Went Supergroup
items.text: In 2012, Depp co-founded the rock supergroup Hollywood Vampires with Alice Cooper and Aerosmith's Joe Perry, releasing two albums together. A decade later he teamed up with legendary guitarist Jeff Beck for the duo album 18, writing two original songs and touring Europe with Beck as his guitarist.

images.caption: Co-founded Hollywood Vampires with Depp in 2012.
Recorded and toured with Depp right up until Beck's death in 2023.
